gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 8-port KVM costs per computer with host cables counted: TESmart's HKS801-P23 is $399 / 8 = $49.88 per PC (4K60 4:4:4, USB 3.2 Gen 1, all 8 HDMI+USB KVM cables in the box), and the StarTech R8AD122 that ChatGPT showed as its pro pick ships with no cables at all and only a USB 2.0 hub.
standout_why: I compared officekithq.com (lists which kits include cables, gives no prices), mamalinux.com (TESmart 8X1 at $229 with eight 5 ft cables, MT-VIKI at $114 and ANGEET at $129.99, all 4K30 or USB 2.0 budget units; no TESmart 4K60/USB 3 unit and no StarTech), virtual-pc.com (no prices), workcocoon.com (only two 4-port units, price bands only), dockgearhq.com HDMI (ATEN CS18208 with no price; cables listed as 'Not confirmed') and kvmswitchtech.com (Cyberview enterprise units at $746 to $2,459). None works out cost per computer for a 4K60 USB 3 8-port, and none says the StarTech R8AD122 ships without cables. Mamalinux has part of the idea: it prices the 4K30 USB 2.0 TESmart and lists its cables.
decides: This confirms the TESmart HKS801-P23 as the pick for 8 PCs at 4K60 with USB 3, and it takes the shine off ChatGPT's StarTech 'professional' card. The StarTech's price doesn't include the 8 DisplayPort and 8 USB host cables, and its shared hub is USB 2.0, so it costs more per computer and does less. The HKS801-L23 ($18.00 per port on sale) only makes sense if 4K30 is enough. The HKS801-M24 ($74.88 per port) is worth it only for HDMI 2.1 (4K144/8K60). One caution: the maker's page showed the P23 as sold out with 'Notify me'.
